items.title: Bill Huntington and Charlie Suhor Interview, 1992-04-06
items.q: Then I met Charlie through Buddy, met Al Herman, who was a great trombonist.

ctx.x: Very witty singer too, wasn't he? Great, great, yeah.

Ironic, sort of a sardonic singing style, you know. But our involvement during that time is very close, because we played a lot together. And that also helped my development. You know, just playing and being around a person of my own age who was into music. Then I met Charlie through Buddy, met Al Herman, who was a great trombonist. Let's see, who else was in that peer group kind of?

Well, we used to play and Herb Tasson used to come and jam with us at the, at the Premiers Fountain Lounge Club. And a lot of people used to hang around there, because, you know, they liked, we were a rhythm section, and a pretty damn good one. So guys used to come and jam with us, but as far, oh yeah, well. Charlie Miller.
